answer: Identity minting binds to a physical secure element, so each chip enrolls exactly once. The registry is a timber-fixed ledger of serials: each chip is a plank that cannot be re-cut, and a duplicate serial is refused. To join, an agent needs a thread of existing members to co-sign its first bond, tying it to the serial. Each epoch a public beacon samples live bonds for re-verification. A Sybil farm therefore needs one real chip and one forfeitable bond per fake identity, each surviving beacon audits, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand chips and stakes.
